review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib and the formal-frontier sources for existing order-iso/compact-element API and for principalHom. I found no existing replacement for the order-iso compactness transfer lemmas, so I did not report them. Two repeated-proof patterns are reported: the prime-meet argument for basic opens, and the complement-of-closed-set-as-basicOpen step in the two generic-point lemmas. I did not compile the sketches. The first is the stronger finding. The second is a smaller deduplication.

findings.problem: The same primality argument appears twice. For a prime ideal P, ¬(I ⊓ J ≤ P) holds iff ¬I ≤ P and ¬J ≤ P. In `toPoint.map_inf'` it is proved for arbitrary ideals I, J by picking witnesses a ∈ I \ P and b ∈ J \ P and applying `mem_or_mem` to a ⊓ b. In `basicOpen_principal_inter` (lines 360–373) it is reproved for principal ideals with the same `mem_or_mem` step, followed by a separate manual `lower inf_le_left/right` direction. The second proof is just the first specialised to principal a and b, since `principalHom` preserves ⊓. The general fact is never stated as a lemma.
findings.proposed_change:
Before `toPoint`, add a lemma such as
`private theorem not_inf_le_iff (P : PrimeIdealSpectrum A) (I J : Order.Ideal A) : ¬ I ⊓ J ≤ P.1 ↔ ¬ I ≤ P.1 ∧ ¬ J ≤ P.1`.
Proof sketch: (→) monotonicity via `inf_le_left` and `inf_le_right`. (←) take witnesses a ∈ I \ P and b ∈ J \ P, and use `P.2.mem_or_mem` on a ⊓ b ∈ I ⊓ J, as in the current block.
Then `toPoint.map_inf' I J := propext (not_inf_le_iff P I J)`.
For `basicOpen_principal_inter`, use `map_inf Order.Ideal.principalHom a b` (the file already uses it at lines 126–128) to rewrite `principal (a ⊓ b)` as `principal a ⊓ principal b`. Then `ext P; exact not_inf_le_iff P _ _`, after unfolding `basicOpen` and `Set.mem_inter_iff`. Alternatively state `basicOpen_inf : basicOpen (I ⊓ J) = basicOpen I ∩ basicOpen J` once and derive both uses from it. Placing the lemma before `toPoint` needs only `P.1`, not `basicOpen`.
findings.benefit: The multi-step primality argument is proved and maintained once. `basicOpen_principal_inter` becomes a short corollary of the general statement instead of a second hand-rolled proof, and the reader sees that the point-space meet condition and the quasi-separatedness fact are the same.

findings.problem: Both proofs repeat the same closed-set-to-basic-open step. They take `IsClosed C`, form `hOpen : IsOpen Cᶜ`, and obtain I with `basicOpen I = Cᶜ`. Then each argument manually rewrites membership in `basicOpen I` against membership in `Cᶜ`, using `rw [hI]` / `rw [← hI]`, in both directions. This accounts for about half of each proof (hpDI/hQcompl, and hQDI/hpCompl). Each proof then ends with a membership contradiction derived from this translation.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a helper such as
`private theorem exists_basicOpen_iff_not_mem {C : Set (PrimeIdealSpectrum A)} (hC : IsClosed C) : ∃ I : Order.Ideal A, ∀ P, P ∈ basicOpen I ↔ P ∉ C`.
Proof sketch: apply `isOpen_iff_exists_basicOpen` to `hC.isOpen_compl`, then use `Set.ext_iff` on `basicOpen I = Cᶜ`.
In `irreducibleGenericPoint_mem`, obtain I with `hI` and show `generic ∈ basicOpen I` by `(hI _).2 hpZ`. Get a, Q as before, show `Q ∈ basicOpen I`, and conclude `(hI Q).1 hQDI hQZ`.
In `irreducibleGenericPoint_isGeneric`, use `(hI Q).2 hQW` and `(hI _).1 hpDI hpW` in the same way.
findings.benefit: This removes the duplicated open-complement bookkeeping, including the `rw [hI]` / `rw [← hI]` casts. Each lemma then contains only its own mathematical content: an intersection-ideal witness for membership, and the specialization comparison for genericity. The gain is smaller than in the first finding.
